title: Mr. Keen, Tracer of Lost Persons
paragraphs: A long-running detective drama about the kindly but persistent Mr. Keen, a professional tracer who searches for missing people and becomes involved in mysteries surrounding their disappearances.
Long-running Hummert detective property derived from Robert W. Chambers’ 1906 The Tracer of Lost Persons.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Early tracer / serial era (October 12, 1937 to December 31, 1943) and Half-hour case era in surviving archive (January 6, 1944 to April 19, 1955).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Anne Hummert (producer, creator, and writer), Frank Hummert (producer, creator, and writer), [[person|bennett-kilpack|Bennett Kilpack]] (performer), Larry Elliott (announcer), Lawrence Klee (dialogue writer, performer, and writer), Phillip Clarke (performer), and Richard Leonard (director).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

The stories often return to murder and homicide, family, marriage and domestic conflict, missing persons and disappearances, inheritance, wealth and family property, kidnapping and unlawful confinement, and wartime industry, sabotage and national defense.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Whitehall and rotating sponsor commercial-radio model, Wartime domestic-security story context, Serial-to-standalone detective format evolution, and Extreme survival scarcity from a long-running radio property.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-big-show|The Big Show]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|dragnet|Dragnet]], [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]], and [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]].
plain_text:
A long-running detective drama about the kindly but persistent Mr. Keen, a professional tracer who searches for missing people and becomes involved in mysteries surrounding their disappearances.

Long-running Hummert detective property derived from Robert W. Chambers’ 1906 The Tracer of Lost Persons.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Early tracer / serial era (October 12, 1937 to December 31, 1943) and Half-hour case era in surviving archive (January 6, 1944 to April 19, 1955).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Anne Hummert (producer, creator, and writer), Frank Hummert (producer, creator, and writer), Bennett Kilpack (performer), Larry Elliott (announcer), Lawrence Klee (dialogue writer, performer, and writer), Phillip Clarke (performer), and Richard Leonard (director).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to CBS Radio Network.

The stories often return to murder and homicide, family, marriage and domestic conflict, missing persons and disappearances, inheritance, wealth and family property, kidnapping and unlawful confinement, and wartime industry, sabotage and national defense.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Whitehall and rotating sponsor commercial-radio model, Wartime domestic-security story context, Serial-to-standalone detective format evolution, and Extreme survival scarcity from a long-running radio property.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include The Big Show, Columbia Workshop, Dragnet, Duffy's Tavern, and Fibber McGee and Molly.
